targets.title: Expand Implement maintained internal logic for '.' (server)
targets.rationale: Implement status-zero cancellation handling in the XHR lifecycle, preserve successful file reads through request, origin, and response URL evidence, and reuse browser-style URL preprocessing in the existing malformed-protocol guard.
uncertaintyReasons: Browser event ordering, validateStatus bypass, relative URLs, and file-protocol exceptions interact at the adapter boundary.

targets.title: Expand Create represented unit tests for '.' (server)
targets.rationale: Create the represented browser and isolated-adapter regression coverage for canceled HTTP requests, file reads, responseURL absence, validateStatus bypass, page origins, and URL preprocessing.
uncertaintyReasons: Fresh-module browser globals and a faithful XHR stub add setup complexity beyond the individual assertions.

targets.title: Modify Author and verify maintained repository documentation
targets.rationale: Document the user-visible cancellation correction, compatibility rationale, error code, validateStatus behavior, and retained file-protocol exceptions in the maintained prerelease changelog.
uncertaintyReasons: The note is concise but must state browser-version and compatibility details accurately.

targets.title: Understand the bounded change specification
targets.rationale: Understand XHR completion and cancellation ordering, Axios settlement semantics, browser URL preprocessing, and the legitimate status-zero file cases before choosing the rejection boundary.
uncertaintyReasons: The defect depends on a browser-specific event-shape change plus cross-environment file behavior.

targets.title: Review and integrate the completed change
targets.rationale: Review error compatibility, cleanup ordering, protocol precedence, file exemptions, shared normalization, and the two levels of regression coverage as one adapter change.
uncertaintyReasons: A false rejection of a valid status-zero environment would be a meaningful compatibility regression.

targets.title: Validate and harden the completed change
targets.rationale: Exercise the adapter across canceled HTTP requests and all represented file URL sources, confirming the expected error code, cleanup, and settlement behavior independently from test authoring.
uncertaintyReasons: Browser and simulated-XHR behavior may differ enough to require debugging or an additional compatibility check.

targets.title: Add maintained artifact 'lib/helpers/normalizeURLForProtocolCheck.js'
targets.rationale: Extract the bounded WHATWG-style leading-control and tab/newline normalization helper with non-string pass-through so protocol checks share one maintained implementation.
uncertaintyReasons: Control-character handling must match URL preprocessing closely enough for both existing validation and the new adapter use.

targets.rationale: Introduce a shared safe property write and integrate it into interpreted object parsing, generated fast paths, asynchronous results, and finite-key record parsing without slowing ordinary keys unnecessarily.

targets.title: Expand Implement represented validation behavior for '.' (application)
targets.rationale: Define and implement the security-sensitive boundary: declared __proto__ is retained as an own data property while inherited setter invocation and prototype pollution remain impossible.

targets.title: Modify Implement represented CI/CD and infrastructure configuration
targets.rationale: Update the release workflow's TypeScript matrix and build ordering so the shipped build is exercised under the represented compiler versions without the former special-case comments and fail-fast override.
uncertaintyReasons: The workflow edit is compact, but package-manager ordering and compiler compatibility affect a release gate.

targets.title: Understand the bounded change specification

targets.title: Review and integrate the completed change

targets.title: Validate and harden the completed change

targets.title: Expand Create represented unit tests for '.' (library)
targets.rationale: Add a detached-method regression that also proves the mapped tasks share the limiter's concurrency accounting, preserve order, and receive iterable values and indexes.

targets.title: Expand Implement maintained internal logic for '.' (library)
targets.rationale: Remove the mapped helper's dynamic receiver dependency by closing over the owning limiter while preserving existing scheduling and result semantics.
uncertaintyReasons: The code change is one expression, but it must retain a shared limiter rather than create independent scheduling.

targets.title: Understand the bounded change specification
targets.rationale: Understand the public method's receiver-independent contract and how map work participates in the limiter's shared concurrency state.

targets.title: Review and integrate the completed change

uncertaintyReasons: A focused review should confirm the fix does not accidentally bind to another limiter instance.

targets.title: Validate and harden the completed change
targets.rationale: Exercise attached and detached calls together under a low concurrency limit and check scheduling, ordering, and results independently from test creation.
uncertaintyReasons: Asynchronous ordering can expose a subtle test or implementation mistake despite the tiny patch.

targets.title: Expand Create represented unit tests for '.' (library)
targets.rationale: Add regressions for hooks that replace normalized Headers with either a new Headers instance or a plain object, proving custom and JSON content headers survive the request pipeline.
uncertaintyReasons: Both replacement shapes must reach the same serialized request behavior without coupling the test to implementation details.

targets.title: Expand Implement maintained internal logic for '.' (library)
targets.rationale: Re-normalize headers after the onRequest hook and move the normalization boundary so later body processing and dispatch always receive a Headers instance.
uncertaintyReasons: Hook ordering and body-dependent content-type insertion must remain unchanged for existing callers.

targets.title: Understand the bounded change specification
targets.rationale: Understand the request option normalization sequence, mutation rights of onRequest hooks, and when JSON body logic relies on Headers methods.
uncertaintyReasons: The correct normalization point depends on the hook contract and downstream body handling.

targets.title: Review and integrate the completed change
targets.rationale: Review hook mutability, header normalization, content-type behavior, and coverage for both supported replacement forms.
uncertaintyReasons: The main review risk is an ordering regression for request bodies or later hooks.

targets.title: Validate and harden the completed change
targets.rationale: Exercise hook-replaced headers with JSON and ordinary request paths, confirming dispatch receives normalized headers and preserves user values independently from test authoring.
uncertaintyReasons: A downstream fetch implementation may expose normalization differences not visible in unit assertions.
